document.title: Harakat ul-Ansar: Increasing Threat to Western and Pakistani Interests (DI TR 96-008)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Secret] Pakistan's ISID provides at least $30,000 and possibly $60,000 per month to Harakat ul-Ansar, though Pakistan may be trimming support to avoid state-sponsor listing. HUA is reaching out to bin Laden and Qadhafi and shifting toward Western targets; contacts hinted at attacks on civilian airliners.

events.description: HUA began kidnapping Westerners; at least 13 people kidnapped in four incidents since early 1994.
Coup attempt against the Pakistan Army/civilian government; HUA elements reportedly participated.
Al-Faran hostages probably killed on 13 December after Indian forces killed the kidnappers' leader earlier that month.
Lajpat Nagar market bombing in New Delhi killed 13; the Jammu and Kashmir Islamic Front possibly assisted by HUA.
CIA Directorate of Intelligence publishes the report DI TR 96-008.
HUA began kidnapping, taking at least 13 people (12 Westerners) in four incidents by 1996.
Coup attempt against the Pakistan Army/civilian government in which HUA elements reportedly participated.
Indian security forces killed the leader of the Al-Faran kidnappers.
Four Western hostages held by Al-Faran/HUA were probably killed.
Lajpat Nagar market bombing in New Delhi killed 13; the JKIF may have been assisted by HUA/Pakistan.

key_claims: The HUA is shifting from attacking Indian forces in Kashmir to targeting Westerners and civilians outside Kashmir.
The four Western Al-Faran hostages were probably killed on 13 December 1995.
Pakistan appears to be scaling back HUA support to avoid being named a state sponsor of terrorism.
The HUA may turn to Bin Ladin and Qadhafi for funds, which could encourage attacks on US targets.
A crackdown by Islamabad could make Pakistan an HUA target, given anti-government sentiment among HUA leaders.
The HUA may be preparing to attack civilian or VIP aircraft in India.
